'''Kiyoshi Nagai''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} (June 25, 1949 – September 27, 2019) was a Japanese [[Structural biology|structural biologist]] at the [[MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology]] Cambridge, UK. He was known for his work on the mechanism of [[RNA splicing]] and structures of the [[spliceosome]].

== Education ==
Nagai studied at [[Osaka University]] and earned a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] under the supervision of Hideki Morimoto working on the [[Allosteric regulation|allosteric]] effect in [[hemoglobin]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Galej|first1=Wojciech P.|last2=Toor|first2=Navtej|last3=Newman|first3=Andrew J.|last4=Nagai|first4=Kiyoshi|date=2018-04-25|title=Molecular Mechanism and Evolution of Nuclear Pre-mRNA and Group II Intron Splicing: Insights from Cryo-Electron Microscopy Structures|journal=Chemical Reviews|volume=118|issue=8|pages=4156–4176|doi=10.1021/acs.chemrev.7b00499|issn=1520-6890|pmid=29377672}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
In 1981 Nagai moved to the [[Laboratory of Molecular Biology|MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology]] where he worked as a post-doc with [[Max Perutz]] on overproduction of eukaryotic proteins in ''[[Escherichia coli|E. coli]].''<ref name=":0" /> He produced recombinant [[hemoglobin]] and studied its properties and evolution by crystallography and mutagenesis.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nagai|first1=K.|last2=Thøgersen|first2=H. C.|date=1984|title=Generation of beta-globin by sequence-specific proteolysis of a hybrid protein produced in Escherichia coli|journal=Nature|volume=309|issue=5971|pages=810–812|issn=0028-0836|pmid=6330564|doi=10.1038/309810a0|bibcode=1984Natur.309..810N|s2cid=4307749}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nagai|first1=K.|last2=Perutz|first2=M. F.|last3=Poyart|first3=C.|date=1985|title=Oxygen binding properties of human mutant hemoglobins synthesized in Escherichia coli|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|volume=82|issue=21|pages=7252–7255|issn=0027-8424|pmc=390827|pmid=3903751|doi=10.1073/pnas.82.21.7252|bibcode=1985PNAS...82.7252N|doi-access=free }}</ref> In 1987 he became a tenured group leader at the LMB and was joint head of the Division of Structural Studies from 2000 to 2010. He was appointed fellow of [[Darwin College, Cambridge]] in 1993.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.darwin.cam.ac.uk/people/fellows|title=Master & fellows {{!}} www.darwin.cam.ac.uk|website=www.darwin.cam.ac.uk|access-date=2018-12-09}}</ref>

In 1990 his group solved the first structure of an [[RNA recognition motif|RRM]] (RNA recognition motif) protein, [[Small nuclear ribonucleoprotein polypeptide A|U1A]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nagai|first1=K.|last2=Oubridge|first2=C.|last3=Jessen|first3=T. H.|last4=Li|first4=J.|last5=Evans|first5=P. R.|date=1990-12-06|title=Crystal structure of the RNA-binding domain of the U1 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein A|journal=Nature|volume=348|issue=6301|pages=515–520|doi=10.1038/348515a0|issn=0028-0836|pmid=2147232|bibcode=1990Natur.348..515N|s2cid=4336326}}</ref> and in 1994 showed how it specifically binds RNA.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Oubridge|first1=C.|last2=Ito|first2=N.|last3=Evans|first3=P. R.|last4=Teo|first4=C. H.|last5=Nagai|first5=K.|date=1994-12-01|title=Crystal structure at 1.92 A resolution of the RNA-binding domain of the U1A spliceosomal protein complexed with an RNA hairpin|journal=Nature|volume=372|issue=6505|pages=432–438|doi=10.1038/372432a0|issn=0028-0836|pmid=7984237|bibcode=1994Natur.372..432O|s2cid=9404488}}</ref> Subsequent work involved [[X-ray crystallography|crystallographic]] studies of other components of the [[spliceosome]], a large macromolecular machine that catalyses [[RNA splicing]] in [[eukaryote]]s, including components of the [[U2 spliceosomal RNA|U2 snRNP]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Price|first1=S. R.|last2=Evans|first2=P. R.|last3=Nagai|first3=K.|date=1998-08-13|title=Crystal structure of the spliceosomal U2B"-U2A' protein complex bound to a fragment of U2 small nuclear RNA|journal=Nature|volume=394|issue=6694|pages=645–650|doi=10.1038/29234|issn=0028-0836|pmid=9716128|bibcode=1998Natur.394..645P|s2cid=204999419}}</ref> and the Sm proteins<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kambach|first1=C.|last2=Walke|first2=S.|last3=Young|first3=R.|last4=Avis|first4=J. M.|last5=de la Fortelle|first5=E.|last6=Raker|first6=V. A.|last7=Lührmann|first7=R.|last8=Li|first8=J.|last9=Nagai|first9=K.|date=1999-02-05|title=Crystal structures of two Sm protein complexes and their implications for the assembly of the spliceosomal snRNPs|journal=Cell|volume=96|issue=3|pages=375–387|issn=0092-8674|pmid=10025403|doi=10.1016/S0092-8674(00)80550-4|s2cid=17379935|doi-access=free}}</ref> and culminating in the crystal structures of the full [[U1 spliceosomal RNA|U1 snRNP]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Pomeranz Krummel|first1=Daniel A.|last2=Oubridge|first2=Chris|last3=Leung|first3=Adelaine K. W.|last4=Li|first4=Jade|last5=Nagai|first5=Kiyoshi|date=2009-03-26|title=Crystal structure of human spliceosomal U1 snRNP at 5.5 A resolution|journal=Nature|volume=458|issue=7237|pages=475–480|doi=10.1038/nature07851|issn=1476-4687|pmc=2673513|pmid=19325628|bibcode=2009Natur.458..475P}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kondo|first1=Yasushi|last2=Oubridge|first2=Chris|last3=van Roon|first3=Anne-Marie M.|last4=Nagai|first4=Kiyoshi|date=2015-01-02|title=Crystal structure of human U1 snRNP, a small nuclear ribonucleoprotein particle, reveals the mechanism of 5' splice site recognition|journal=eLife|volume=4|doi=10.7554/eLife.04986|issn=2050-084X|pmc=4383343|pmid=25555158 |doi-access=free }}</ref> and the [[U5 spliceosomal RNA|U5 snRNP]] components [[Prp8]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Galej|first1=Wojciech P.|last2=Oubridge|first2=Chris|last3=Newman|first3=Andrew J.|last4=Nagai|first4=Kiyoshi|date=2013-01-31|title=Crystal structure of Prp8 reveals active site cavity of the spliceosome|journal=Nature|volume=493|issue=7434|pages=638–643|doi=10.1038/nature11843|issn=1476-4687|pmc=3672837|pmid=23354046|bibcode=2013Natur.493..638G}}</ref> and Brr2.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nguyen|first1=Thi Hoang Duong|last2=Li|first2=Jade|last3=Galej|first3=Wojciech P.|last4=Oshikane|first4=Hiroyuki|last5=Newman|first5=Andrew J.|last6=Nagai|first6=Kiyoshi|date=2013-06-04|title=Structural basis of Brr2-Prp8 interactions and implications for U5 snRNP biogenesis and the spliceosome active site|journal=Structure|volume=21|issue=6|pages=910–919|doi=10.1016/j.str.2013.04.017|issn=1878-4186|pmc=3677097|pmid=23727230}}</ref>

From 2014, Nagai's group used [[Cryogenic electron microscopy|cryo-electron microscopy]] to study the spliceosome. Structures of the U5.U4/U6 tri-snRNP gave the first structural insights into the assembly of the spliceosome.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nguyen|first1=Thi Hoang Duong|last2=Galej|first2=Wojciech P.|last3=Bai|first3=Xiao-chen|last4=Savva|first4=Christos G.|last5=Newman|first5=Andrew J.|last6=Scheres|first6=Sjors H. W.|last7=Nagai|first7=Kiyoshi|date=2015-07-02|title=The architecture of the spliceosomal U4/U6.U5 tri-snRNP|journal=Nature|volume=523|issue=7558|pages=47–52|doi=10.1038/nature14548|issn=1476-4687|pmc=4536768|pmid=26106855|bibcode=2015Natur.523...47N}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nguyen|first1=Thi Hoang Duong|last2=Galej|first2=Wojciech P.|last3=Bai|first3=Xiao-Chen|last4=Oubridge|first4=Chris|last5=Newman|first5=Andrew J.|last6=Scheres|first6=Sjors H. W.|last7=Nagai|first7=Kiyoshi|date=2016-02-18|title=Cryo-EM structure of the yeast U4/U6.U5 tri-snRNP at 3.7 Å resolution|journal=Nature|volume=530|issue=7590|pages=298–302|doi=10.1038/nature16940|issn=1476-4687|pmc=4762201|pmid=26829225|bibcode=2016Natur.530..298N}}</ref> Nagai's subsequent structures of spliceosomes in various stages of assembly and catalysis<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fica|first1=Sebastian M.|last2=Nagai|first2=Kiyoshi|date=2017-10-05|title=Cryo-electron microscopy snapshots of the spliceosome: structural insights into a dynamic ribonucleoprotein machine|journal=Nature Structural & Molecular Biology|volume=24|issue=10|pages=791–799|doi=10.1038/nsmb.3463|issn=1545-9985|pmid=28981077|pmc=6386135}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Scheres|first1=Sjors Hw|last2=Nagai|first2=Kiyoshi|date=2017|title=CryoEM structures of spliceosomal complexes reveal the molecular mechanism of pre-mRNA splicing|journal=Current Opinion in Structural Biology|volume=46|pages=130–139|doi=10.1016/j.sbi.2017.08.001|issn=1879-033X|pmid=28888105}}</ref> combined with structures from the groups of [[Reinhard Lührmann]], [[Shi Yigong|Yigong Shi]] and others have provided crucial insight into the catalytic mechanism of pre-mRNA splicing.

* 2000 [[Novartis Medal and Prize|Novartis Medal]] of the Biochemical Society<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nagai|first1=K.|last2=Muto|first2=Y.|last3=Pomeranz Krummel|first3=D.
